text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.9% today to $140.44, continuing a sharp two-day rally that has erased most of a six-day decline. The move follows statements from President Trump on November 10th that the Iran conflict is "going to be ending fairly soon" and that Iran is "militarily effectively over"—comments that reduced immediate geopolitical risk and supported oil prices, which climbed back above $107 globally. With crude gaining ground on de-escalation hopes, energy stocks like ConocoPhillips have rebounded in tandem.

The stock's recovery also reflects a broader whipsaw in the energy sector tied to shifting geopolitical bets. Earlier in the week, reports of Iran tensions and military threats sent crude below $90, but Trump's more dovish rhetoric has reversed that trade, at least for now. The gap between US oil ($99.64) and global Brent ($107.03) also widens ConocoPhillips' margin on international operations, providing additional tailwind.
